title: Refuse a small-or-larger cap that names no execution worker, unless the inline run is recorded
action: AGENTS.md says cells from small up run through dispatched workers and never zero execution workers, but nothing reads the registry at cap. In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs the lane branch at about line 289 (where small/standard/high-risk already require non-empty files_changed) gains a second check: the capping cell's trace.worker must appear in state.json workers[] with a matching cell id. When it does not, refuse - naming the cell, the worker in the trace, and the two ways forward: dispatch the cell to a registered worker (bee state worker add --nickname N --cell ID --tier T --status running, the shape written by packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/state_group/workers.rs), or re-run finish with a new --inline-reason "<why>" flag that records the named deviation in the cell trace as inline_reason. tiny is unaffected: it may run inline by contract. Red-first: write the refusal test and the inline-reason escape test before the check exists, and keep every existing cap test green - several cap cells with no registered worker and will need --inline-reason or a registered one.

truths: a small+ cap with no registered worker for that cell is refused
--inline-reason caps and records the reason in the trace
a registered worker caps with no flag
